compiled_state.description:
## The defect

`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml`, the `sandbox-enforcement` job, discards ALL output from
its two `apt-get` calls:

```
339:  docker run --rm --privileged ubuntu:24.04 bash -c '
340:    set -e
341:    apt-get update -qq >/dev/null 2>&1
342:    apt-get install -y -qq bubblewrap >/dev/null 2>&1
343:    bwrap --version
```

With `set -e`, a failure in either line aborts the container and the step fails with apt's exit
code and **nothing whatsoever in the log** to say what went wrong. `2>&1` sends stderr to
`/dev/null` too, so even the error message is gone.

## Observed, 2026-09-05

Change 2652's `sandbox enforcement (Linux bwrap, gating)` cell — a GATING cell — failed with
`exit code 100`. 100 is apt-get's generic error. The log contains no apt output at all, so the
failure could not be diagnosed from it. It was ultimately triaged as a transient package-manager
fault only by inference: the step reads nothing from the patchset (stock container, Ubuntu
archive), the change touched only `tests/`, `docs/` and a YAML comment, and the same job had been
`success` on run `33938327905` eight minutes earlier. That is circumstantial reasoning standing in
for evidence the step deliberately threw away.

## Why this one is worth fixing rather than tolerating

Read the job's own comment at `:301-305`. It explains that this job exists precisely BECAUSE the
previous arrangement produced an unreadable signal:

> "those runners deny unprivileged CLONE_NEWUSER, so `probe()` returns None, every enforcement
> test SKIPS, and the leg goes green having proven nothing — the signal for a broken sandbox is
> indistinguishable from the signal for a healthy one."

The job written to remove an indistinguishable signal contains its own indistinguishable signal.
When it fails, "the Ubuntu archive was briefly unavailable" and "bubblewrap has been removed from
the archive" and "the container image changed under us" all look identical: `exit code 100`.

It is also a GATING cell, so an unreadable failure blocks every change on that patchset while
giving no one anything to act on.

## The fix is small and the tradeoff is real

`-qq` already suppresses routine chatter; the `>/dev/null 2>&1` on top of it is what removes the
diagnostics. The obvious change is to drop the redirection (keeping `-qq`), or to keep stdout
quiet while letting stderr through (`>/dev/null` without `2>&1`), so a failure explains itself
while a success stays terse. The reason someone wrote it this way — apt is noisy and this is a hot
gating path — is legitimate, so the fix should preserve quiet-on-success rather than simply
deleting the redirect and accepting the noise.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A failing `apt-get` in this job leaves its error message in the CI log. Proven by
      deliberately breaking the install (e.g. an unresolvable package name) and reading the
      captured output, not by asserting the redirect was removed.
- [ ] A SUCCESSFUL run stays as quiet as it is today — no regression into a wall of apt output on
      the hot gating path. Proven by comparing log length on a green run before and after.
- [ ] The same audit is applied to the rest of this job and its siblings: any other
      `>/dev/null 2>&1` on a command whose failure would abort a gating step is either justified
      in a comment or fixed. Enumerate what you found and its disposition — do not fix only the
      two lines named here.
- [ ] The job's existing comment at `:301-305` is extended (or a new one added) noting that its
      own diagnostics must stay readable, so the next person tightening this path does not
      reintroduce the silence for the same good reason.
compiled_state.title: The gating bwrap sandbox job discards all apt output, so an apt failure aborts it with exit 100 and no explanation -- inside a job whose own comment exists because an unreadable signal was the previous bug
